title: Pivoting from Web to App | Replit to ?
author: Shnatrix
selftext:
Hey guys,

I've been TRYING and I mean REALLY trying to build this game in replit however due to fluxuating screen sizes every time the game tries to adjust to the resolution of the window it's playing in the text goes fuzzy. I tried vector text but still doing it which is likely a setting that's been coded in and really I'm starting to think this would be easier to trash and start again - I've spent probably close to $1k in replit so far trying to get it to work but it just can't get it to go.

So would I be better off trying to build it somewhere else and have it as a downloaded game and your save info is stored on-line.

What I ultimately want to build is my version of a web3 game (Not specifically web3ish). I want to hide real life items of value in the game. That will sit in loot tables for players to pick up, get back to town and redeem. I just think it's cool, and there will be DLC and other things that will give people ways to pay into the game to fund the items I'm putting in for others to get out.

I'm not looking to get rich off this, just want to make something fun for a community and try and remove the stigma of web3...

Also you'll be able to mint and sell items for ingame currency that I'll set up as a crypto currency - hence the web3 aspect of it. Again as a way of making a small amount of money to make the prize draw bigger and cooler.

The game in it's broken state is at gemforgechronicles com if you want to look at it as is.

But is it wiser to change tack from web game to app?

comments.author: CulturalFig1237
comments.body: If your core goal is community and accessibility, staying on the web makes more sense. Apps add friction, installs, updates, and platform rules. I would try to fix the rendering problem first before committing to a full pivot.

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body: Thank you! I've tried a lot tbh, but maybe I just rebuild it as a web app, with different rules when I build. But good call for making it more user friendly

comments.author: fatboyor
comments.body:
I am curious - the issue is that web based has rendering issue, any other issue you see?  
  
I tried '1-click game generating' platforms out there, they mostly generate garbages that's not iteratable and lack those nuance level of constraints provided by mature game engine ( e.g. if i zoom out all assets, should zoom out proportionally, easy things like this )   
  
Are you using any game engine or completely vibe code using html + js? sorry have not used replit before.

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body:
It's purely vibes, it's a pixel game, which I did for ease. But the scaling is the issue. For reasons you've pointed out.

It's phaser, vite, js - those are just words I see replit saying tbh
